title: On Criticising the plan in the open letter
subtitle: 文学写作 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 文学写作（人与社会·文学艺术与体育·文学与写作）
meta: 主题语境：文学写作（人与社会·文学艺术与体育·文学与写作）　|　核心词汇：criticise　|　正文 355 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 criticise 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1983 the painter ① criticised the plan in the open letter on the same day, and every visitor in the studio said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three seasons on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the painter ② criticises the plan in the open letter before dawn without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ criticise the plan in the open letter at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ criticised the plan in the open letter before — a line in the catalogue for May 1977 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Criticising the plan in the open letter on the same day, the painter said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the brush at the far easel, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ criticise the younger painters fairly before dawn, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Criticise the younger painters fairly at once and never mention it again.

By 1990 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the catalogue, and a new visitor from the next studio ⑧ criticises the younger painters fairly on the same day every season without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the easel, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ criticised the plan in the open letter again when nobody else would.

⑩ To criticise the plan in the open letter, my mother said in 1995, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the studio remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the studio forgets, somebody criticises the plan in the open letter before dawn again and somebody must criticise the plan in the open letter on the same day all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 批评（一般过去式 criticised the plan in the open letter：1983 年画师头一回这样做，当天就）
B. v. 批评（一般现在 criticises the plan in the open letter：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 批评（不定式 to criticise the plan in the open letter：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 批评（过去完成时 had criticised the plan in the open letter：1977 年五月的展品目录上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 批评（动名词 criticising the plan in the open letter 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 评论（criticise the younger painters fairly：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去评论对年轻画家作出公允评价）
G. v. 评论（criticise the younger painters fairly：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 批评（后段两处：新来的观者照例 criticises the younger painters fairly，而母亲又一次 criticised the plan in the open letter）

answers.why: criticise 意为“批评”，1983 年画师当天就批评在公开信里批评那方案，那是画室里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 criticised。
criticise 意为“批评”，自那以后画师天没亮就把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 criticises。
criticise 意为“批评”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯批评在公开信里批评那方案”，此处为不定式 to criticise the plan in the open letter。
criticise 意为“批评”，展品目录里 五月 那行字说明早在 1990 年之前就有人批评过，故用过去完成时 had criticised。
criticise 意为“批评”，画师说“批评在公开信里批评那方案这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 criticising the plan in the open letter 作主语。
criticise 意为“评论”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去评论对年轻画家作出公允评价”，should ever 之后用原形 criticise the younger painters fairly。
criticise 意为“评论”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻评论对年轻画家作出公允评价（criticise the younger painters fairly at once），以后再也不要提起。
criticise 意为“批评”，新来的观者每个季度都照例评论对年轻画家作出公允评价，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 criticises。
criticise 意为“批评”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次当天就批评在公开信里批评那方案，用一般过去式 criticised 叙述。
criticise 意为“批评”，结尾那句是母亲 1995 年的话：要批评在公开信里批评那方案，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和画室记住的那一件。

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 criticise 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1983 the painter criticised the plan in the open letter on the same day, and nobody in the studio forgot it.
Even now the painter criticises the plan in the open letter before dawn whenever the studio asks.
Criticising the plan in the open letter on the same day, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever criticise the younger painters fairly before dawn, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new visitor from the next studio criticises the younger painters fairly on the same day every season, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother criticised the plan in the open letter again, and the studio remembered that half.
